The FOMC statement points to solid activity and a strengthening labor market while inflation remains below 2 percent, consistent with an accommodative, gradualist stance. The October 2017 Beige Book corroborates modest-to-moderate growth but highlights binding labor shortages—especially in construction and transportation—that are restraining some business expansion and exacerbating hurricane recovery in the Richmond, Atlanta, and Dallas Districts. Wage pressures are stronger in those sectors, yet broader price pressures remain modest. Household/retail spending increased across several Districts, but this is tempered by SLOOS evidence of tighter consumer credit and softer loan demand. Net: growth-positive but capacity and credit constraints argue for a slightly more cautious tilt than before.
